knowledge_base.answer: No: copying all 315 trades with 10000 of fake money would have ended at 9765.86 (-2.34%) after costs, while buying and holding the S&P 500 (SPY) gained 19.64%. The test also relied on guesses, such as assumed exits on 137 day trades, $1000 assumed on 199 entries with no share count, and half the position assumed sold on 202 trims, and options were not tested at all. The course itself says you don't have to take every trade [LPP-AVOID-2], so copying every post is not how it tells you to trade, and past results don't predict future ones. Not advice.

root_cause.cluster: failures in LPP session extractor v1 on path tool_call>reasoning>tool_call>final_answer (Task Completion, Error Handling)
root_cause.prism_cause: Prompt: detectors failed_tool_call fired in 25 of 25 runs and unsupported_answer in 20 of 25 (both decisive)
root_cause.our_sentence: The v1 prompt let the model quote long caption stretches and lose track of open positions, so most v1 runs failed a code check.

evaluator.name: Numbers grounded
evaluator.checks: Every price, level and quantity appears in the quote it cites
evaluator.inputs: The same 30 LPP sessions (proof set), scored by PRISM
evaluator.caveat: PRISM's judge saw a cut-off run output in 24 of 30 v1 runs and 24 of 30 v2 runs, so its score can't separate the versions; our code check reads the full output.

code_mirror.what: The same rule run by our code on the same sessions, as a cross-check

failed_runs.what: Agent runs in PRISM where any event failed a code check

evaluator.framing: The v2 fix shows in extraction quality (grounded numbers, fewer failed runs), not in money: on the same sessions both versions end within a few dollars. Part of v2's gain is code (quote trimming, a position-ledger rule), not only the prompt.

evaluator_verdict.name: Verdict numbers from results
evaluator_verdict.checks: Every number in the verdict is in the results file; it cites a card and says Not advice
evaluator_verdict.inputs: The same 4 results files: cryptowizard/v1, lpp/v1, lpp/v2, ziptrader/v1

code_mirror.what: Our code checks (check_numbers, check_cites, check_language) on the same runs
